newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia allows pension funds to invest in funds.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia allows pension funds to invest in funds.

text.p: Indonesia's Finance Ministry said on Thursday that pension funds would now be allowed to invest in open and closed-end funds.

The ministry said in a statement obtained by Reuters that both open and closed-end funds are sufficient to improve the wealth of pension funds. The funds invest mainly in fixed income paper, with the balance in stocks and time deposits.
"The Finance Ministry hereby has decided to allow pension funds to invest in these funds," it said.
Pension funds were previously only allowed to invest in time deposits, certificate of deposits, shares, bonds and other papers listed on the exchanges except warrants and options.
They were also allowed to invest in money market papers issued by Indonesian corporations.
The new decree said pension funds can invest all their capital in open and close-end funds, but they are allowed to only place up to 10 percent of their money into any one fund.
